en.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
en.about: A standing hip hinge with a dumbbell in each hand: you push your hips back to lower the weights with a flat back and soft knees, then stand tall. It builds strength in the hamstrings, glutes and lower back.
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms straight and your palms facing your body.
Bend your knees slightly, brace your core and draw your shoulders back and down.
Push your hips back to hinge forward, keeping your back flat and your knees softly bent.
Lower the dumbbells close to your legs until you feel a stretch in your hamstrings, usually around knee to mid-shin height.
Keep your neck in line with your back by looking at the floor, not ahead or into a mirror.
Push your heels into the floor and drive your hips forward to stand tall, keeping your back flat.

mistakes.says: Lower back rounds as you lower. Keep your back flat and go only as low as you can without it rounding.
Knees bend too much and it turns into a squat. Keep a slight bend and move by pushing your hips back.
Dumbbells drift away from your legs. Keep them close to your thighs and shins on the way down and up.
Dumbbells are too heavy to keep your back flat. Choose a weight you can lower with a flat back on every rep.
You look up or into the mirror. Keep your neck in line with your back and look at the floor as you hinge.

cautions: Bending from a rounded lower back instead of your hips can seriously injure the low-back muscles. Hinge from your hips and keep your back flat.
